guidance: A mowing plan for the one-third rule, not a turf diagnosis. The height a lawn tolerates depends on species, season, shade and water; do not mow wet grass, keep the blade sharp and check the deck height on a hard surface. A thinning, diseased or newly seeded lawn may need renovation rather than a sequence of cuts.
method: The one-third rule says no single mowing may remove more than one-third of the leaf tissue, so the height after a cut must be at least two-thirds of the height before it, and a lawn kept at 3 in is cut when it reaches 4.5 in. From that, the minimum number of passes is the smallest n with (2/3)^n x current <= target. The greedy plan cuts as deep as the rule allows each time: pass k leaves max(target, (2/3)^k x current), the last pass lands exactly on the target, and each pass reports the depth it removes and that depth as a percentage of the height before it. A target at or above the current height returns no cut and the height at which to mow next, 1.5 x target. Heights are accepted from 0.5 to 24 in (1.3 to 61 cm); the ratios are unit-free, so inches and centimeters produce the same plan. Numbers accept a decimal comma and spaces, and refuse signs, exponent notation and text. The page makes no network requests and stores nothing.
